sections.content: How many people are "police officers (sergeant and below)"?

146,080 people

were counted on the census as "police officers (sergeant and below)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Police officers (sergeant and below) investigate crimes, patrol public areas, arrest offenders and suspects and enforce law and order.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "police officers (sergeant and below)", 16.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "police officers (sergeant and below)" was 65 years or older.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "police officers (sergeant and below)" there were more men than women (65.8% compared with 34.2%).

This means "police officers (sergeant and below)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "protective service occupations".

Men made up 65.8% and women made up 34.2% of "police officers (sergeant and below)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "police officers (sergeant and below)" included:

  • IT project managers
  • footwear and leather working trades
  • managers and directors in the creative industries

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "police officers (sergeant and below)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "police officers (sergeant and below)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "police officers (sergeant and below)", 7.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (95.4% compared with 4.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99.4%) than self-employed (0.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
